evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.72, whose reaction arrow is labelled 'r 2H'. The drawn precursor is R-CH(H)-CH(H)-CH2-Y'-C(R')=Y(+.): the n-ionized carbonyl heteroatom Y carries the printed '+.', the two hydrogens that migrate are written out as explicit H letters on the two chain carbons, and the bond that is cleaved -- the alkyl C-Y' bond -- is marked with a WAVY line. Book draws 0 curved arc(s) / fishhooks; the only graphical mechanism markers are the two explicit H letters, the wavy cleavage mark and the 'r 2H' label, so every encoded move is curator-supplied. Products as printed: the odd-electron neutral .CnH2n-1 and the EVEN-electron ion HY'-CR'=YH+, which the page draws together with its resonance partner HY'=CR'-YH+ joined by a double-headed arrow (one localized form, HO-C(CH3)=OH+, is encoded consistently; the partner is not). ENCODING NOTE (honest divergence): both migrating hydrogens are invisible to the bond bookkeeping because RDKit folds a mapped explicit H into implicit valence, so each H transfer is written as the single electron relocation it produces at the heavy-atom level. Move <1> is the first rearrangement (H from C(6) to the carbonyl oxygen O(2) through the drawn six-membered array Y-C(1)-Y'(4)-C(5)-C(6)-H): net effect, the odd electron moves from O(2) to C(6). Moves <2,3> are the ensuing cleavage of the marked C(5)-Y'(4) bond with formation of the C(5)=C(6) pi bond. Move <4> is a bookkeeping composite for the second rearrangement: the second electron of the cleaved C-O bond and the electron of the second migrating hydrogen pair up in the new Y'-H bond, leaving the odd electron on C(7); since neither the C(7)-H nor the O(4)-H bond exists in the mapped SMILES, this shows up as one fishhook from the cleaved bond to C(7). INSTANTIATION: Y = Y' = O, R' = CH3, alkyl = n-butyl (R = CH3), i.e. n-butyl acetate, the textbook r2H case: the ion is the protonated acid CH3C(OH)2+ (m/z 61) and the neutral is the resonance-stabilized C4H7. radical. The page writes the neutral generically as .CnH2n-1, so the chain length is deliberately unspecified in the figure. NO PRINTED NUMBERS on p.191: detected=false, status 'inferred', no relative_intensity; m/z 61.0284 is computed for this instantiation.

(2) The generic double-hydrogen family h2Transiton_1/2/3 targets the whole r2H, and h2Transiton_1 '[H]1[C]2([H]3)[C]4[_A]5[C]6([C]7){=}[_A+.]8>>[C.]2([H]3)[C]4[_A]5[C]6([C]7){=}[_A+]8[H]1' again matches move <1>. RULE MISMATCHES, reported rather than smoothed over: (a) h2Transiton_3 '[C.]2([H]3)[C]4[_A]5[C]6([C]7){=}[_A+]8[H]1>>[C]2{=}[C]4.[H]3[_A+.]5{=}[C]6([C]7)[_A]8[H]1' takes the SECOND hydrogen off the radical-bearing carbon itself (the page takes it from the next carbon along, the one drawn with the second explicit H), and it lands the odd electron on the ION ('[_A+.]5'), producing an odd-electron protonated-acid ion and a closed-shell alkene neutral -- the exact opposite of the page, which prints an EVEN-electron ion HY'-CR'=YH+ and an odd-electron neutral .CnH2n-1. Its atom/charge/spin COUNTS balance, so the conservation guardrail cannot catch it. (b) IMS_4_46_rH_2 '[H]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[O]5[C]6([C]7){=}[O]8[H]9>>[C]2[C.]3[C]4.[H]1[O+]5{=}[C]6([C]7)[O]8[H]9' (indexed under equation 4.46) produces the right protonated-acid ion but its neutral fragment '[C]2[C.]3[C]4' forms NO pi bond at the carbon that lost the hydrogen, leaving an unsatisfied valence there instead of the CnH2n-1 unsaturation the page requires; MOD's H-explicit term graphs do not check valence, so this too survives the guardrail. (c) IMS_4_46_rH_1 '...>>[H]1[C]2[C.]3[C]5[O+]6[C]7([C]8){=}[O]9[H]4' puts the charge on the ester oxygen while leaving the carbonyl oxygen with a double bond AND a hydrogen, i.e. a neutral trivalent oxygen.
